author: George Orwell
fact_sheet_notes: 10 chapters total.
Old Major dies THREE NIGHTS after his speech (not three days).
Napoleon took NINE puppies in Ch 3, raised them in a loft above the harness room. They reappear as NINE dogs with brass-studded collars in Ch 5.

Napoleon's signal to the dogs is described as a 'strange whimper' (not specifically 'high-pitched' — lessons calling it 'high-pitched whimper' are quoting direct from the novel text, which is acceptable).

Battle of the Cowshed (Ch 4): Snowball receives a wound from Jones's shotgun (grazes his back). One sheep is killed. Boxer knocks a stable boy unconscious (the boy later revives and runs away). Snowball and Boxer both receive 'Animal Hero, First Class'. The dead sheep receives 'Animal Hero, Second Class'.
Snowball studied Julius Caesar's campaigns — confirmed.
Commandment 4 altered to 'No animal shall sleep in a bed WITH SHEETS' (Ch 6).
Commandment 5 altered to 'No animal shall drink alcohol TO EXCESS' (Ch 8, after Napoleon gets drunk).
Commandment 6 altered to 'No animal shall kill any other animal WITHOUT CAUSE' (Ch 7, after purges).
Hens' rebellion (Ch 7): NINE hens die over the five-day standoff.
Ch 7 purges: FOUR PIGS confess first, then other animals (hens, sheep, goose etc).
'Beasts of England' banned Ch 7, replaced by Minimus's song 'Animal Farm, Animal Farm / Never through me shalt thou come to harm!'
Mr Whymper introduced Ch 6 — described as a solicitor, not just a broker.
Moses returns in Ch 9, given beer allowance (not 'beer ration of one glass per day' — pigs get a pint each, Napoleon a half-gallon; Moses just gets a small daily beer).
Boxer is promised retirement at AGE TWELVE.

Van reads 'Horse Slaughterer and Glue Boiler' — some editions say 'Alfred Simmonds, Horse Slaughterer and Glue Boiler' (this name is in the novel text but not confirmed/denied by SparkNotes/LitCharts summaries).
Final scene: Napoleon and PILKINGTON both play ace of spades and quarrel. Napoleon announces farm will revert to 'Manor Farm'.
Napoleon's titles in Ch 8 include 'Father of All Animals', 'Terror of Mankind', 'Protector of the Sheep-fold', 'Ducklings' Friend'.

Orwell's 'Why I Write' (1946): 'every line of serious work that I have written since 1936 has been written, directly or indirectly, against totalitarianism and for democratic Socialism.' Also: 'Animal Farm was the first book in which I tried, with full consciousness of what I was doing, to fuse political purpose and artistic purpose into one whole.'
Orwell completed Animal Farm in Feb 1944 (written 1943-44). T.S. Eliot at Faber rejected it. Published by Secker & Warburg August 1945.
Orwell born Eric Arthur Blair 1903, died 1950.
Sugarcandy Mountain: 'clover was in season all the year round, and lump sugar and linseed cake grew on the hedges' (not just sugar — linseed cake too).
Napoleon has a food taster appointed AFTER the purges (Ch 8).

lessons.title: The Battle of the Cowshed & Snowball's Leadership

issues.claim: The lesson says Boxer 'knocking a stable boy unconscious with his hoof' and that he was 'distressed, thinking he has killed the boy'. The stable boy was not killed — he revived and ran away. The lesson correctly says Boxer thought he killed him (not that he actually did), so this is accurate.
issues.correction: No correction needed — the lesson correctly represents Boxer's belief vs reality.
issues.source: SparkNotes Ch 4: 'Boxer mournfully paws at a stable boy who appears to be dead and insists that he didn't mean to kill anyone.' The boy later revives.

issues.claim: The lesson says 'A decoration that Napoleon will later claim for himself' re: Snowball's Animal Hero First Class medal. Napoleon does not take Snowball's medal; he later wears his own Animal Hero medals in Ch 7. This is a minor inaccuracy — Napoleon doesn't claim the medal but does claim credit for the battle.
issues.correction: Napoleon doesn't physically take Snowball's medal. He rewrites history to claim he was the hero of the battle. Remove or clarify 'A decoration that Napoleon will later claim for himself.'
issues.source: SparkNotes/LitCharts Ch 7: Napoleon wears his own medals; he rewrites history about the battle but does not take Snowball's medal.

lessons.notes: Snowball studying Julius Caesar's campaigns — confirmed. Two-phase strategy (feigned retreat then ambush) — accurate per SparkNotes. Snowball awarded Animal Hero First Class, wounded by Jones's shotgun — confirmed. One sheep killed — confirmed.

lessons.title: Napoleon's Cult of Personality

issues.claim: The lesson states Napoleon's poem by Minimus 'is inscribed on the barn wall alongside a portrait of Napoleon, REPLACING the Seven Commandments as the farm's central text.' This is factually wrong. The poem is inscribed at the OPPOSITE END of the barn from the Seven Commandments — the commandments are not replaced at this point in Ch 8. The commandments are still on the wall (albeit altered). The final reduction to one commandment happens in Ch 10.
issues.correction: Change 'replacing the Seven Commandments as the farm's central text' to 'placed at the opposite end of the barn from the Seven Commandments' or 'displayed prominently alongside a portrait of Napoleon'.
issues.source: SparkNotes Ch 8: 'Napoleon caused it [the poem] to be inscribed on the wall of the big barn, at the opposite end from the Seven Commandments.' LitCharts confirms the poem and commandments coexist on the barn wall in Ch 8.

issues.claim: The lesson says Napoleon 'always enters from a different door to the other pigs.' This is a minor detail that may be an embellishment — SparkNotes/LitCharts do not confirm this specific detail for Ch 8. Napoleon is described as living in greater luxury and rarely appearing in public, but the 'different door' detail is not clearly in the source summaries.
issues.correction: Flag for verification against the novel text. If not in the text, remove.
issues.source: Not confirmed in SparkNotes or LitCharts Ch 8 summaries.

lessons.title: Chapters 9-10: The Betrayal Complete

issues.claim: The lesson states 'A van arrives bearing the words "Alfred Simmonds, Horse Slaughterer and Glue Boiler." Boxer is being sent to the knacker's.' This is accurate — 'Alfred Simmonds' is in the novel. However, the lesson then says 'Benjamin, who has remained cynically silent throughout the novella, reads the lettering on the van aloud.' In the novel, Benjamin calls out to alert the other animals after reading the van — but the lesson says 'The animals rush to the van, calling to Boxer. Boxer tries to kick his way out but is too weak.' This account in the Key Fact box is accurate.
issues.correction: No correction needed on this specific point.
issues.source: Confirmed accurate.

issues.claim: The lesson states that in Ch 10, 'the pigs now walk on two legs, wear clothes and carry whips. The sheep have been taught a new slogan: "Four legs good, two legs better!"' — this is accurate. However, the lesson also says 'The windmill is built but used to mill corn for profit, not to ease the animals' workload as Snowball promised.' This is an important nuance: Snowball originally promised the windmill would provide electricity and reduce working hours. The lesson correctly represents this betrayal of the promise.
issues.correction: No correction needed.
issues.source: LitCharts Ch 10 confirms.

issues.claim: The lesson says 'The farmhouse, which was supposed to be "preserved as a museum" after the Rebellion, has become the pigs' private quarters.' This is confirmed accurate — the animals resolved after the Rebellion that the farmhouse would be preserved as a museum.
issues.correction: No correction needed.

issues.claim: The lesson says 'Napoleon bans "Beasts of England" and replaces it with a new anthem PRAISING HIM.' Napoleon's personal praise poem (also by Minimus, titled 'Comrade Napoleon') is a separate poem inscribed on the barn wall in Ch 8. The banning of 'Beasts of England' and the new anthem replacement happen in Ch 7.

key_findings: AQA L08 (Napoleon's Cult of Personality, b3e6ed27): HIGH — States Minimus's poem 'replaces the Seven Commandments' on the barn wall. Factually wrong: in Ch 8, the poem is inscribed at the OPPOSITE END from the commandments. The commandments are still present and are only replaced by the single final commandment in Ch 10.

OCR L04 (Chapters 7-8, 6e95a98a): MEDIUM — States 'Beasts of England' is replaced by 'a new anthem praising him [Napoleon]'. The replacement song (by Minimus) praises Animal Farm, not Napoleon personally. Napoleon's personal praise poem ('Comrade Napoleon') is a separate Ch 8 item.

Edexcel L06 / AQA L06 character analysis: MEDIUM — Napoleon described as having 'food tasters' as a general character trait. Food taster is only introduced in Ch 8; acceptable in character summary context but worth noting the chronology.

AQA L04 (Battle of Cowshed, bdfda3aa): LOW — Implication that Napoleon 'later claims' Snowball's Animal Hero First Class medal is inaccurate. Napoleon rewrites history about the battle but does not physically take Snowball's medal.
Edexcel L02 and OCR L02: LOW — Both say Old Major died 'three days after his speech'. The novel text says 'three nights later'. Minor imprecision.
AQA L09 (Boxer's death, a2589a87): LOW — States Boxer is 'twelve years old' when he collapses. The text says he is 'approaching' the retirement age of twelve, not that he has reached it.
No lessons contain errors about the Seven Commandments themselves, the Battle of the Cowshed outcome, the identity of key characters, the chapter sequence of major events, or the final scene.

All allegorical mappings (Napoleon=Stalin, Snowball=Trotsky, Old Major=Marx/Lenin, Squealer=Pravda, Boxer=proletariat, Benjamin=cynical intellectuals, Mollie=bourgeoisie, dogs=NKVD, Moses=Orthodox Church) are standard and correct throughout all 26 lessons.
